notes: Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue scheme '<row number><bank>.<letter>' where the image's numbered rows are the 'column' and letters a-e are bank t, f-j are bank b.

The ground rail used is the right-hand rail column next to the '+' label in the picture; all ground rail connections use tn.N ports, which are one strip. The specific N values are only distinct hole labels, not exact positions.
Amber LED is modelled as type led with colour=amber, since no amber LED type exists.
Buzzer port 1 is taken as the positive leg (the '+' mark in the image, wired to GPIO15 via the blue wire); port 2 goes to the ground rail.
The Pi-side end of each male-to-female jumper is port 'a' (female, onto the header); port 'b' is the male end in the breadboard. GND.1 is taken as the physical pin 6 ground.
The pushbutton straddles the centre gap: side 1 on row 28 (e/f), side 2 on row 30 (e/f). Row 28 goes to ground and row 30 goes to GPIO21.
Each LED has its own 330R resistor between the GPIO jumper row (d/e) and the LED anode row (h/j); LED cathodes go to the ground rail.
Setup note: the Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorising in claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. They were not needed for this task.
